patch_description: Restructured around a "worst-triangle feedback loop" architecture: each iteration computes all 286 triangle areas once (vectorized cross products, cheaper and more stable than Heron), identifies the k smallest triangles, and only proposes moves to vertices of those worst triangles — pushing a vertex away from its opposite edge, which is the direct geometric gradient direction for increasing a degenerate triangle's area. Data flow is organized as: seed bank → coarse ring-annealing → targeted worst-triangle relaxation → fine greedy polish → hull-normalization. Moves that shrink hull area also help the ratio, so hull area is recomputed incrementally only when a hull vertex moves. This focuses all compute on the binding constraints (the minimal triangles) instead of wasting evaluations on random vertices, improving min_area_normalized at similar runtime.
